title: GitHub repository policy
description: Machine-readable statement of the branch governance and Actions concurrency policy applied to the GitHub repositories this account owns. It is the only place that answers what a governed repository's default branch is protected by; scripts render GitHub ruleset payloads from it and diff them against the live API. Silence is not an answer here: every object closes with additionalProperties:false and every decision that could be read either way — strict status checks, per-repository context resolution, whether a workflow may be cancelled — is stated explicitly, so an omitted key is a schema error rather than an implied 'no'.

version.description: Content version of this policy. Bumped on every change, per the _contract canonical-config pattern, so a consumer can tell whether the policy it applied is the policy that is written down.

defaults.description: Values every ruleset inherits unless it restates them. Present so the ~DEFAULT_BRANCH targeting decision is written once.

required_checks.description: How required status-check contexts are resolved, and the strictness decision. Contexts themselves live per repository — a context name is a CI job name, and a job name that does not exist in a repo blocks every pull request in it forever.

source.description: Only one resolution strategy is permitted. A global context list is a footgun, not a convenience, so the schema refuses to express one.

default_contexts.description: Contexts applied to a repository with no override. Must be empty: a repository nobody has vetted gets protection, not a gate on checks it may not produce.

integration_id.description: GitHub App id that produces the checks (15368 = GitHub Actions). A context without it matches any producer, which lets an unrelated app satisfy a required check.

strict_required_status_checks_policy.description: 'Require branches to be up to date before merging'. Pinned false by the schema, not merely defaulted, because turning it on makes N merges cost O(N^2) CI runs under the parallel-worker/one-PR architecture. Flipping it requires editing this schema, which is the point.

strict_is_intentional.description: A required acknowledgement that the false above is a decision. Its only purpose is to make a well-meaning 'fix' impossible to land silently.

do_not_enforce_on_create.description: Whether the check requirement is waived on branch creation. True lets a repository be seeded before CI exists.

rulesets.description: The ruleset set, in apply order. Safety first: it depends on nothing and is applicable to a repository on its first day, while the PR/CI ruleset presumes a workflow exists.

repositories.description: Per-repository overrides keyed by owner/repo. Absence is meaningful and safe: the repository inherits the rulesets with an empty context list.

actions.description: The GitHub Actions concurrency standard and the workflow classification a script uses to decide where it may be applied.

cancel_superseded_pr_runs.description: Account-wide default for whether cancellable workflows get the cancelling concurrency block. Overridable per repository.

comment.description: Provenance or rationale carried in-band, following the settings.d fragment convention. Never consumed as data.

refName.description: A ref pattern. Only GitHub's magic refs are allowed — a literal branch name would be wrong on the repositories that spell their default branch the other way, and would stop matching the day one is renamed.

bypassActors.description: Actors permitted to bypass the ruleset. Empty is the policy; it is written out rather than omitted so that an actor added on github.com shows up as drift instead of as an unmodelled field.

key.description: Stable local identifier. Scripts address rulesets by key; `name` is the human label that appears on github.com and may be re-worded.

allOf.$comment: required_status_checks must state both toggles and must carry an empty context array — contexts are per repository, never global.
pull_request must answer every review question. An omitted review toggle reads as 'no' on the API but as 'undecided' to a reader, and those are different things.

required_review_thread_resolution.description: The load-bearing review gate on a solo account: with zero required approvals, an unresolved thread is the only thing that can block a merge.

allOf.$comment: Rules with no parameters must not invent any.

repositoryOverride.description: What differs for one repository. Every field is optional because the absence of an override is itself a well-defined state — inherit — unlike the absence of a policy decision.

contexts.description: CI job names that must pass. Each is paired with the account-wide integration_id when the ruleset payload is rendered.

disable.description: Canonical rules this repository opts out of. Opting out is visible and reviewable here; it is not something a script may infer.

pattern.description: Case-insensitive regex tested against the lowercased workflow file content. Stored lowercase; no inline flags, so jq, grep -E and python re all agree on it.

apply_concurrency.description: Whether a cancelling concurrency block belongs on workflows in this class.

concurrency_ref.description: Which block under `actions` this class uses. A reference, so the group expression is written once.

name_patterns.description: Case-insensitive regexes tested against the lowercased workflow name and filename.

precedence.description: Pinned. A workflow matching both classes is never_cancel: a serialized test run costs minutes, a cancelled deployment costs a half-written external state.

unclassified_action.description: What to do with a workflow matching neither class. Only 'report' is expressible — guessing on an unknown workflow is how a migration gets cancelled mid-run.
